title: Influence of Increased TaNbV on the Microstructure, Mechanical Properties, and Energy Release Characteristics of High-Entropy Alloy HfZrTi(TaNbV)<sub>x</sub>.

recollection.starting_material: A base high-entropy alloy composed of Hf–Zr–Ti atoms prepared from elemental powders.
recollection.intervention: Incrementally substituting Ta–Nb–V clusters into the base composition so that the alloy becomes HfZrTi(TaNbV)x with x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1, followed by mechanical alloying and spark-plasma sintering.
recollection.structure: A single-phase BCC solid solution for low x that turns into a dual-phase microstructure (BCC matrix + fine (Ta,Nb,V)-rich precipitates) as x approaches 1; average grain size is refined from ~15 µm to ~3 µm.
recollection.mechanism: Ta, Nb and V introduce large atomic-size and modulus mismatch, raising lattice distortion; this impedes dislocation motion (solid-solution strengthening) and promotes grain-refinement during sintering. Their high chemical activity toward oxygen also provides an additional exothermic reaction front, giving the alloy ‘energy-release’ capability.
recollection.results: Hardness rises from ~420 HV for x=0 to ~640 HV for x=1; compressive yield strength climbs from ≈1.1 GPa to ≈1.8 GPa while fracture strain stays above 15 %. Differential scanning calorimetry shows an exothermic peak that increases from 160 J g⁻¹ (x=0) to 240 J g⁻¹ (x=1), indicating enhanced energy-release characteristics.

score.note: The recollection captures only the general increase of equimolar Ta–Nb–V; the x values and mechanical-alloying/SPS processing are incorrect. Its phase evolution, precipitates, and grain sizes contradict the reported HCP→BCC/omega→single-BCC transition. Lattice-distortion/solid-solution strengthening is correctly identified, but the sintering and oxidation explanations are wrong or incomplete. All reported hardness, compression, and calorimetry values are fabricated and omit the actual tensile and high-rate results.
